prompt: A car purchased for $\$24{,}000$ loses $12\%$ of its value each year. Which expression represents the car's value, in dollars, after $t$ years?
hint: The car loses part of its value each year, so think about the part it keeps. That kept fraction is the yearly multiplier.

hints.text: The car loses part of its value each year, so think about the part it keeps. That kept fraction is the yearly multiplier.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Try a round number: $\$100$ losing $10\%$ leaves $\$90$, so the multiplier is $0.90 = 1 - 0.10$. Subtract the loss rate from $1$ to get the base of the decay model.
Keeping $100\% - 12\% = 88\%$ means multiplying by $0.88$ each year. Apply that multiplier $t$ times to the starting value $24000$.
Multiplying by $0.88$ a total of $t$ times gives $24000(0.88)^t$, which is choice C.

learningObjective: Build an exponential decay model from a percent loss.
explanation: Losing $12\%$ of the value leaves $88\%$ of it, so each year the value is multiplied by $0.88$.
Applying that multiplier once per year for $t$ years gives $24000(0.88)^t$.
Choice A keeps only $12\%$ each year, choice B makes the value grow, and choice D subtracts a fixed $12$ cents a year.
The correct expression is $24000(0.88)^t$, which is choice C.

alternativeExplanations.title: Check the first year
steps: After one year the car should be worth $24000 - 0.12(24000) = 24000 - 2880 = \$21{,}120$.
Building the expected first-year value before you look at the choices is the fastest way to handle every model-selection question.

alternativeExplanations.title: ⚠️ The trap here
steps: Choice A keeps 12% each year instead of losing it — a car worth $346 after two years should fail your sniff test.
Build the multiplier from what REMAINS: 1 − 0.12 = 0.88. Then sanity-check year one: 24,000 × 0.88 = 21,120, a plausible used-car value.
